books.title: The Hobbit
books.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
books.note: A tidy hole: comfort disturbed, terror endured underground, treasure won, home returned to a little wider than it was.

books.title: The Lord of the Rings
books.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
beats: The Ring revealed at Bag End
books.note: Two lines that share a shape until the last mile: the world climbs back to peace but Frodo cannot, and the shape of victory is measured by who does not come home.

books.title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
books.author: J.K. Rowling
beats: Voldemort on the back of a head
books.note: Vonnegut's Cinderella in a school uniform: cupboard-floor to castle-peak, one plunge at the climax, and a coronation before summer.

books.title: The Hunger Games
books.author: Suzanne Collins
books.note: A hole where the recovery is barbed: survival, yes, but as a Capitol target — the exit sits below where the story started.

books.title: The Martian
books.author: Andy Weir
beats: I'm going to have to science the shit out of this
books.note: A hole worn down by sawtooth: every clever fix invites the next failure, so the axis oscillates through the descent and rise both.

books.title: Life of Pi
books.author: Yann Martel

axes.label: What actually happened on that lifeboat

beats: Alone on the lifeboat with Richard Parker
The algae island and the human tooth
Mexican shore; the tiger walks off without looking back
Second story to the Japanese investigators
books.note: The rescue is real but the certainty isn't: two accounts, one lifeboat, and the reader is asked which story they prefer.

books.title: The Kite Runner
books.author: Khaled Hosseini
beats: There is a way to be good again
For you, a thousand times over
books.note: A decades-wide hole with a damped exit: the debt is paid partially and late, and the ending resolves not to joy but to the smallest possible relief.

books.title: The Road
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
beats: The family with the children takes the boy
books.note: A dark flat band the length of the book with one candle at the end; the recovery is not a rise, it is a refusal to go all the way to zero.

books.title: Never Let Me Go
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro

axes.label: What Kathy and the reader understand about Hailsham

beats: Madame flinches from them at the fence
Miss Lucy: you're told and not told
The Cottages, and what donation means
Madame confirms the deferral was a rumor
books.note: The quietest scissors in fiction: knowledge climbs the whole book while fortune sinks, and neither line ever raises its voice.

books.title: Atonement
books.author: Ian McEwan

axes.label: Robbie and Cecilia (as the novel presents it)
Whether the reunion we just read is true

beats: Briony misreads the fountain and the library
Robbie is taken away in the police car
Briony visits Cecilia and Robbie in Balham
London 1999: they both died in the war
books.note: The rise you read in Part Three is the atonement itself — a fiction — and Part Four collapses fortune and certainty in the same vertical stroke.

books.title: The Handmaid's Tale
books.author: Margaret Atwood

axes.label: Whether Offred's fate can be known

beats: Historical Notes: no record either way
books.note: The line hovers in a low band the whole book; at the last minute the van erases certainty itself — rescue and arrest sharing the same door.

books.title: Gone Girl
books.author: Gillian Flynn

axes.label: What the reader knows about Amy

beats: Nick looks guilty from every angle
Cool Girl monologue: Amy is alive and framing him
Amy kills Desi and returns as a hero
The pregnancy locks the marriage shut
books.note: A vertical mid-book snap on knowledge: the reader is dragged up to a truth Nick still cannot escape, and his line stays underground.

books.title: And Then There Were None
books.author: Agatha Christie

axes.label: Guests still alive on Soldier Island
What the reader can tell about the killer

beats: Down to Vera and Lombard on the beach
Vera hangs herself under the noose Wargrave left
books.note: Two staircases in opposite directions: the survivor count steps down while reader knowledge steps sideways, and only the confession letter lets knowledge finally leap.

books.title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
books.author: Agatha Christie

axes.label: What the reader knows about the murder
Trust in Dr. Sheppard, the narrator

beats: Ackroyd found stabbed in his study
Ralph Paton missing — the obvious suspect
Poirot: the narrator is the murderer
books.note: The reader climbs a staircase of clues with a friendly narrator, then discovers at the top that the ladder itself was the confession.

books.title: Rebecca
books.author: Daphne du Maurier

axes.label: What the narrator understands about Rebecca

beats: Maxim confesses: he hated her, he killed her
Dr. Baker: Rebecca had cancer, wanted death
Manderley in flames on the horizon
books.note: One vertical stroke reorganizes the whole book: everything believed about Rebecca inverts in a single sentence, and the second half is spent replaying the first with new eyes.

books.title: The Da Vinci Code
books.author: Dan Brown

axes.label: What Langdon and the reader piece together
Reader dread as the thriller metronome ticks

beats: Curator dead in the Grand Gallery
The Priory of Sion, and what the Grail actually is
Langdon kneels at the inverted pyramid
books.note: A knowledge staircase climbing steadily while tension sawtooths beneath it — fortune barely moves at all, proof a bestseller can run on axes Vonnegut never named.
